issues.description: The problem statement specifies that a Book struct must have a property named `title` (and `author`, plus optional `genres`), but the solution's Book struct declares the title property as `bookTitle`. Meanwhile the solution's Client and the assembleBookstore factory use `Book(title: ...)` and access `book.title`. This name mismatch between the Book property and its usage will cause compile errors and contradicts the specification that the property be named `title`.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the Book struct's `bookTitle` property to `title` (and ensure its initializer and member label match: `init(title: String, author: String, genres: [Genre]?)`) so it matches the problem specification and the Client/assembler usage. Alternatively, update all usages and initializers to consistently use `bookTitle`, but changing the struct to `title` is recommended to match the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a Book struct with a property named `title`, but the solution defines the same concept as `bookTitle` in Bookstore.swift while Client.swift accesses `book.title`. This inconsistent identifier naming for the same conceptual property (book title) creates mapping confusion and leads to an internal mismatch between the Book type and its usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent property name for the book's title across all artifacts. Rename `bookTitle` to `title` in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift (and update initializers) so it matches the problem statement and Client usage, or alternatively update Client to use `book.bookTitle`. Prefer renaming to `title` to align with the problem description.
